unresolved_risks: The evidence INSERT (BackupCollectService -> BackupJobAuthorizationRepository.record) is a second, separate DB call after JobAdmissionService.submit()'s own commit -- no shared transaction is exposed across the backup-specific service and the generic job-engine admission path, and widening that shared path was out of this movement's named scope. This leaves a narrow window where a REQUESTED job could theoretically be claimed before its evidence row commits. Fail-closed design keeps this safe: BackupJobExecutor treats a missing row as a refusal in every case, so the only possible failure mode is a legitimately authorized job being refused and needing a retry -- never execution without evidence. Flagged for PO awareness.

Claim-time role re-check is 'role:backup_admin has any active binding at all' (RoleBindingRepository.hasAnyActiveBinding), not a full per-actor group-membership RBAC re-evaluation -- that would require RbacEvaluator's LDAP-backed machinery (GroupReferenceCipher, ActorAuthzStateRepository, LocalRoleTokenResolver), which lives in the service module and is not (and architecturally should not become) a worker dependency (13D DS-1/DS-2: service and worker are separate deployable units). The coarse check still correctly refuses the acceptance criterion's own 'role removal' scenario (role_binding_revoke leaving zero active bindings for backup_admin).
